stem:
Neil has a $3$ by $3$ magic square whose magic sum is $15$. He adds $2$ to every entry.

Which claim correctly states what happens?

options.text: Call the answer an entry, and stop at that single cell.
Say the new magic sum $21$ is what creates the add-$2$ change on every entry.
The grid stays a magic square and the magic sum becomes $15 + 3 \times 2 = 21$.
Fill or reject the grid by checking only one row sum of $1$ through $9$, ignoring the add-$2$ transform.

teacher.key_rationale: Adding the same number k to every entry keeps a magic square and raises the magic sum by 3k; here 15+6=21. Naming one entry substitutes the wrong object. Saying the new sum creates the add-2 change reverses the relation. Checking a raw 1–9 fill conflates a different magic-square task.
